newsitem.title: USA: US Apr spot natgas prices rise on storage refills.
newsitem.headline: US Apr spot natgas prices rise on storage refills.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for April 1 edged higher Tuesday, led by an increase in storage injections in the producing and western regions, market sources said.
April Louisiana Gulf prices climbed five cents to the low-$1.80s per mmBtu on most of the pipes, with Henry Hub quoted about five cents over March indices at $1.82-1.87.
In south Texas, April prices rose six cents to the mid-$1.70s. Forecasts for the first few days of April are calling for above- to much above-normal in the Southwest.
For Wednesday delivery, Gulf prices were steady to firmer at $1.86-1.89, while south Texas prices gained about five cents to the low-to-mid $1.80s.

At the New York city-gate, where temperatures are forecast to climb to above normal Wednesday through Friday, swing prices were little changed at $2.16-2.20. April pricing was up about five cents from Monday at $2.14-2.17.
In the Appalachian region, April prices strengthened by about 10 cents to $2.02-2.09, up about 15 cents from March indices.
In West Texas, April 1 Permian prices moved five cents higher to the mid-to-high $1.60s, while swing gas sold in the low-to-mid $1.70s.
At the southern California border, April deals were reported done at $1.75-1.79, up about 15 cents from March indices.
In the Midcontinent, storage replenishment carried April prices into the low-to-mid $1.70s, up about 10 cents from March indices. Swing prices tacked on about two cents to the mid-to-high $1.70s.
Chicago city-gate for next month was quoted at $1.96-2.00, while Detroit city-gate was talked at $2.13-2.15.

Temperatures throughout the Midwest are forecast to remain mostly above normal through Friday, with some areas expected to experience temperatures as much as 15 degrees Fahrenheit above normal by Friday.
Longer-term forecasts into early April show a continuation of normal to above-normal temperatures in the Midwest.
Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from about 30 to 50 bcf, compared with 43 bcf a year ago.
